solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: He is put in ultimate command

indicators.note: the pronoun is placed inside the word for ultimate, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: the ultimate is the best there is
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man is installed at the very top of the chain of command.
explanation.definitionFit: A behest is an order or instruction, as in 'at the king's behest', so it is a command.

clue.text: Meddlesome type engaged young man to protect daughter

parts.note: an engaged telephone line is busy

indicators.note: the boy surrounds and so protects the daughter's letter

parts.note: a boy is a young man

explanation.surface: A nosy person engaged a lad to guard their daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A busybody interferes in other people's affairs, a meddler.

clue.text: Heroin dealer in remarkably well-known band

parts.note: H is slang for heroin

indicators.note: remarkably suggests something done in an unusual way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drug dealer turns up in a famous rock group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkably' works on DEALER IN to give EADLINER after H.
explanation.definitionFit: The headliner is the star act at the top of the bill, typically a famous band.

clue.text: Cries of highly unpleasant Americans, in short

definitions.meaning: SOB is the US abbreviation for son of a bitch, a nasty person

explanation.definitionFit: Sobs are weeping noises, and SOBs is the plural of an abusive American abbreviation.

clue.text: Revolutionary way madman delivers hackneyed tale

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
a nut is slang for a crazy person

explanation.surface: A rebel's lunatic route serves up a tired old story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivers' is only a link between the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An old chestnut is a joke or story repeated so often that it has gone stale.

clue.text: One who shouts out mild expletive encounters extremely little resistance

parts.note: heck is a mild substitute for hell

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: Someone swearing mildly meets hardly any opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: A heckler interrupts a speaker by calling out insults or jeers.

clue.text: U-boat expedition in act of capitulating

parts.note: a U-boat is a German submarine, a sub
a mission is an expedition with a purpose

explanation.surface: A wartime submarine sortie that ends in surrender.
explanation.definitionFit: Submission is the act of yielding or giving in, which is capitulating.

clue.text: Nick Nolte's beginning to upset church

indicators.note: the beginning of the name is its first letter
in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down, so it reads upwards

explanation.surface: The actor Nick Nolte's early career begins to upset the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick Nolte' looks like a name, but 'Nick' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A nick is a small cut, which is also what a notch is.

clue.text: Some accept he is truly godly type

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people do accept that he is a genuinely pious person.
explanation.definitionFit: A theist believes in God, so is a believing, religious sort of person.

clue.text: Dull, vociferous Yankee crushed by leader of Confederates

indicators.note: in a down clue, being crushed by means lying underneath, so the first letter goes above the others
the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: vociferous means loud
Yankee is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for Y

explanation.surface: A loud Union soldier is beaten by the Confederate commander in the American Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloudy day is dull and grey.

clue.text: Confused forgery, with old line written in biro

parts.note: a forgery is a sham, a fake

indicators.note: the two letters are set inside the pen's name, as if written inside it

parts.note: Bic is a famous make of ballpoint pen, and Biro is the British everyday word for a ballpoint

explanation.surface: A puzzled description of a fake document with an old line penned in ballpoint.
explanation.walkthrough: BIC, the pen brand, stands for 'biro' (the British word for any ballpoint); OL goes inside it to give BOLIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Shambolic is British informal for chaotic and disorganised, which is how confused things look.

clue.text: Wash black articles

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
the two English articles, the indefinite 'a' and the definite 'the'

explanation.surface: A laundry note about washing dark-coloured items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' looks like clothing items, but here it means the grammatical articles A and THE.
explanation.definitionFit: To bathe is to wash oneself or something in water.

clue.text: Wolf down sandwich with zero filling

indicators.note: the zero goes inside the sandwich like a filling between slices

parts.note: a BLT is a bacon, lettuce and tomato sandwich
O looks like the figure zero

explanation.surface: Gobbling a sandwich that has nothing at all in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolt food is to eat it very fast, gulping it as a wolf would.

clue.text: Spooner's stuffed snacks for traditional Spanish events

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the first sounds of the two words are exchanged

parts.note: stuffed means full
snacks are bites to eat

explanation.surface: A tapas-style hint at Spain's famous arena spectacles.
explanation.walkthrough: FULL BITES, with the F and B sounds swapped, says BULL FIGHTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bullfighting is a long-standing Spanish tradition held in arenas.

clue.text: Idiot from Northern Ireland and petty officer married on deck

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'on' puts the earlier pieces above the deck

parts.note: a petty officer is an NCO, a non-commissioned officer
the poop is the raised deck at a ship's stern

explanation.surface: A fool from Ulster and a married petty officer, both aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Nincompoop is an informal word for a foolish person.

clue.text: Newton essentially trusted in God's consistency

indicators.note: the two letters go inside the word for God, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: a deity is a god; the possessive simply joins it to the definition
N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its centre, so its middle letter is taken

explanation.surface: Isaac Newton's steady faith in the divine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newton' tempts one to think of Isaac; here it is just the unit symbol N. The middle of 'trusted' is S, and NS goes into DEITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Density is how thick or compact a substance is, which is its consistency.

clue.text: Lodge run by bishop is overlooked

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: the bishop is passed over, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: beside means by, next to
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A house run by a bishop gets ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' looks like a link word for who runs the lodge, but it is the synonym that loses its bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge somewhere is to stay or live there, which is to reside.

clue.text: Guard seen sporting overalls

indicators.note: sporting suggests play and frolic, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A guard is spotted wearing work overalls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sporting' reads as wearing, but it signals an anagram of GUARD SEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungarees are trousers with a bib and straps, a kind of overalls.

clue.text: Hero-worships grown-up defending area north of El Salvador

indicators.note: in a down clue, north of puts the first part above the country code
the adult surrounds the area's letter as if defending it

parts.note: a grown-up is an adult
ES is the international code for El Salvador

explanation.surface: An adult guarding a region somewhere above Central America idolises someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulate someone is to admire them excessively, to idolise them.

clue.text: Fortune-teller poor man called on regular basis

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every second letter of the words is used

explanation.surface: A down-and-out man visits a soothsayer every so often.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of 'poor man called' spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle, like the one at Delphi, foretells the future, as a fortune-teller does.

clue.text: Implement English fellow stuck in hideous crone

indicators.note: the fellow's letter is pushed inside the jumbled letters
hideous suggests something misshapen, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An English chap trapped with an ugly old woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hideous' makes NORCE from CRONE, and 'stuck in' puts F inside it after the N.
explanation.definitionFit: To enforce a rule or law is to put it into effect, to implement it.

clue.text: Rejected son meets Nationalist in central Germany

indicators.note: the nationalist's letter is placed within the other letters

parts.note: the core is the central part of something
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: A disowned son meets a political nationalist in the heart of Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central Germany' looks like one place but is two pieces, CORE and D; N goes inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorned means treated with contempt and spurned, so rejected.

clue.text: Broadcaster claiming Independent politician is inadequate

indicators.note: claiming means taking hold of, so the broadcaster's name surrounds the other letters

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite TV broadcaster
an MP, a Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A TV channel says an independent MP is not up to the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimpy means meagre or too small, so not enough or inadequate.

clue.text: Conserving energy, dogs initially avoided sexual encounters

indicators.note: conserving means keeping inside, so the energy letter is held within
the first letter is missed out

parts.note: corgis are a small breed of dog, famously owned by the late Queen
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Saving energy, the dogs first steered clear of mating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially avoided' drops C from CORGIS, leaving ORGIS, which then holds E.
explanation.definitionFit: Orgies are wild parties involving group sex.

clue.text: Brought back jelly and cake for deprived child

indicators.note: brought back means the word is turned round to run the other way

parts.note: agar is a jelly made from seaweed
a muffin is a small cake

explanation.surface: Someone returned with jelly and cake for a poor child.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragamuffin is a scruffy, ragged child, typically from a poor background.

clue.text: Level area in forest changing hands

indicators.note: the left hand becomes the right, so L is swapped for R

parts.note: a glade is an open space in a forest

explanation.surface: A flat clearing in the woods passes to a new owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing hands' reads as a change of owner, but swaps L (left) for R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: A grade is a level or rank, as in a school grade.

clue.text: Drag from foyer in auditorium

indicators.note: an auditorium is where an audience listens, so the word is as it sounds

parts.note: a hall is an entrance foyer

explanation.surface: Pulling something out of a theatre lobby into the auditorium.
explanation.definitionFit: To haul something is to pull or drag it with effort.

clue.text: Have difficulty saying rude words?

definitions.meaning: to ... words is to pronounce them indistinctly
a ... is an insulting remark; the plural describes what a ... is made of

explanation.definitionFit: Slurring is mumbling speech, and a slur is an insulting remark.

clue.text: Finally found a hotel in satellite state

indicators.note: the three letters are set inside the satellite's name

parts.note: Io is one of the moons of Jupiter

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is used

parts.note: Hotel is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for H

explanation.surface: At last discovering a hotel on a moon.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is a US state in the north-west.

clue.text: Horrendous forty days following outcast's return

indicators.note: following means the second piece comes after the first
a return means the word is read the other way round

parts.note: a leper is a social outcast
Lent is the forty days of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: Lent coming after a pariah comes home is horrible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outcast' is the classic crossword leper, shunned by society; 'return' reverses that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Repellent means repulsive, as horrible as something horrendous.

clue.text: French article on expensive architectural features

indicators.note: in an across clue, 'on' puts the article after the word for expensive

parts.note: a steep price is a high one
les is the French plural definite article

explanation.surface: A French piece about pricey building details.
explanation.definitionFit: Steeples are the tall spires on churches, prominent architectural features.

clue.text: King is taken in by Sunak's figures

indicators.note: taken in means held inside, so the king and 'is' sit within the other piece

parts.note: Rishi Sunak was the UK Prime Minister, a PM, so Sunak's is PM'S
R is from Rex, Latin for king
taken as written

explanation.surface: A monarch is fooled by the Prime Minister's numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' reads like being deceived but means contained.
explanation.definitionFit: Prisms are solid geometric figures with matching ends and flat sides.
